meta.tagline: A postcard wedged between lake and mountain — and the real village behind it

pills: A village of 750, visitors by the million
Whoever stays the night meets the village

overview.title: Welcome to Hallstatt
overview.intro: You've seen the photo of Hallstatt; everyone has. Wooden houses stepping into the lake, the sharp church spire, the wall of the Dachstein behind. What the photo doesn't tell you is this: it is not a set but a real village of 750 people, where salt has been mined for seven thousand years. When the daytime crowds arrive the village becomes a stage; when the boats leave at dusk, the lake stills, the chimneys smoke, and Hallstatt returns to itself. Which Hallstatt you see depends on your clock and your courtesy.

local_word.definition: 'The estate of the salt chamber': the name of the lake district that holds Hallstatt. This one word tells the village's whole story — everything here was built on the white gold inside the mountain.

rules.title: Spend the night
rules.description: The day-trip crowd flows between 10:00 and 16:00; the Hallstatt of 8 am and 7 pm is another place entirely. One overnight stay is the only difference between 'seeing' this village and living it.

rules.title: Remember people live here
rules.description: The house gardens are not photo sets; the villagers are weary of drones and doorstep poses. Respect the quiet hours, keep distance from private homes — you owe courtesy to the people inside the postcard.

rules.title: Don't try to drive into the village
rules.description: The centre is closed to traffic; when car parks P1-P2 fill, the road locks up. The most graceful arrival: train to Hallstatt station, then the ferry across the lake — let your first view come from the water.

tip.label: The Hallstatt philosophy
tip.text: The sights list here is short; the real subject is light. Morning mist, midday clarity, evening gold — the same view changes three times a day. Whoever hurries sees one and misses the other three.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: Hallstatt walks end to end in twenty minutes; the art is arriving — and touring the valley — gracefully.

items.title: Train + ferry — the classic arrival
items.description: From Salzburg or Vienna with a change to Hallstatt station; the little ferry (Stefanie), synchronised with the trains, crosses in 10 minutes. Approaching the village over the water is the trip's first gift.

items.title: Bus link via Bad Ischl
items.description: The bus route with a change at Bad Ischl matches the train in comfort and sometimes beats it in speed; check the Postbus timetable for your evening return.

items.title: If you come by car
items.description: The P1 car park is walking distance from the village and can fill before 9 on summer mornings. Parking in Obertraun and arriving by ferry or bus is your plan B.

items.title: Boats on the lake
items.description: Panoramic lake cruises and Obertraun crossings run in summer; renting a rowboat or electric boat puts you at the calmest viewpoint of all — the middle of the lake.

items.title: Funicular and mountain lifts
items.description: The salt-mine funicular doubles as the lift to the Skywalk terrace; the Dachstein cable car in Obertraun deserves its own day for the ice cave and 5fingers.

callout.label: Ferry tip
callout.text: Photograph the last ferry time on the pier board; it's synced with the trains, but if you miss it, walking around the lake takes well over an hour.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: Hallstatt is tiny, its beds are few and demand is huge: book early and you sleep inside the postcard; book late and you sleep in the neighbouring village — which is no punishment either.

local_word.definition: Austria's traditional inn: restaurant below, rooms above, usually the same family at the helm. Staying in a Hallstatt Gasthof joins you to the village's true rhythm — early breakfast, early quiet.

items.name: Hallstatt Markt — around the square
items.description: The historic houses around the square and the pier: open your window to lake, bells and swans. Very few rooms, high prices, booking months ahead — but at 7 am the square is yours.

items.name: Lahn — the southern quarter
items.description: The flat southern end of the village: near the car park, the lido and the funicular, ten lakeside minutes from the square. Guesthouses are roomier, prices a notch kinder.

items.name: Obertraun — across the lake
items.description: Five minutes by train or boat to the far shore: calm, affordable and at the foot of the Dachstein cable car. It also owns a luxury Hallstatt lacks — the view of Hallstatt itself.

items.name: Bad Goisern — the valley town
items.description: A real town ten minutes down the line: supermarket, bakery, local life. Ideal for the formula of touring Hallstatt by day and returning to small-town calm at night.

items.name: Gosau — the mountain village
items.description: The village of the Gosausee and the Dachstein views: base camp for hikers and skiers. It asks for a car; in return you wake in an alpine meadow.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Hallstatt's four seasons are four different photographs; the crowd is only the season of midday.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Waterfall Season
items.subtitle: Spring · Melting snow, thundering falls
items.description: Snowmelt swells the falls of the Echerntal, the lake turns steel blue, and the crowds stay below summer levels. The airiest window for walking and photography.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May the Waldbachstrub waterfall runs at full roar; the path goes there and back from the square in an hour.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Lake Season
items.subtitle: Summer · Swimming, boats and the midday crush
items.description: The lake warms enough to swim (for the brave), the Lahn lido and boat tours open. The daytime crowd peaks — the morning-and-evening formula saves the day.

callout.label: Midday warning
callout.text: Between 10:00 and 16:00 the square and the photo point are a human river; flee to the mine, the mountain or the far shore in those hours.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Mist and Gold
items.subtitle: Autumn · Morning mist, golden forests
items.description: Morning mist gliding over the lake, forests turning yellow, and thinning crowds: this is the photographer's Hallstatt. In November the village readies for winter and many businesses shutter.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: Cross the lake by ferry on a misty October morning: the village materialises out of the fog like a ghost — often the best frame of the whole trip.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Snowy Tale
items.subtitle: Winter · Snowed roofs, Krampus nights
items.description: Under snow Hallstatt turns surreal; in early December the Krampus runs bring a shivery festival to the village. Day-trippers still come, but the evenings belong wholly to the locals.

callout.label: December note
callout.text: Around December 5-6, fur-clad monsters run the lanes on Krampus nights; frightening for small children, a feast for photographers — plan accordingly.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Hallstatt table is a joint menu of lake and mountain: lake fish on the plate, alpine butter beside it, an imperial dessert to finish.

local_word.definition: The white-fleshed lake fish of the Hallstättersee: from the net in the morning, from the pan at noon. Here 'catch of the day' is not a phrase but the lake's daily report.

items.name: Grilled Reinanke — lake to table
items.description: Served simply with butter and lemon; its freshness asks for nothing else. Eaten on a lakeside Gasthof terrace, the view is included in the dish.
items.tag: Lake fish · on a Gasthof terrace

items.name: Kaiserschmarrn
items.description: The emperor's shredded pancake: a giant dessert with icing sugar and plum compote, the legitimate reward of a mountain walk. Order it for two; it will still disappear.

items.name: Schnitzel with a lake view
items.description: The plate-overflowing veal schnitzel is the national table here too, with potato salad as the classic companion. Eat it in the Gasthof parlour, not the tourist terrace — the difference shows on plate and bill alike.
items.tag: In the Gasthof parlour · with potato salad

items.name: Brettljause — the alpine board
items.description: Mountain cheese, smoked ham, pickles and fresh bread on a wooden board: the Salzkammergut shepherd's supper. Completed with beer or cider (Most).

items.name: The bakery stop — Bad Goisern style
items.description: Fresh pretzels and buttery pastries from the valley bakeries are the local way to start the day; stocks run out early inside Hallstatt, the valley town has more.

items.name: Local beer and Schnaps
items.description: Fresh beer from the lake's own brewers and fruit Schnaps (pear, plum) close the evening. Eye contact during 'Prost' is the Austrian rule.
items.tag: Evening close · Prost with eye contact

callout.label: The terrace rule
callout.text: The lake-front terraces charge a view tax; the same Reinanke one lane inland, in a Gasthof parlour, is both better and kinder on the bill. Save the view for coffee, not dinner.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone knows the postcard spot; these six are the deeper layers of village and valley.

items.name: The Beinhaus — Bone House
items.description: Over 600 skulls painted with flower garlands in the cemetery chapel: a singular tradition born of scarce ground and kept with love. Small, moving, and asking for respect.

items.name: Salzwelten — the salt mine
items.description: The world's oldest salt mine, entered by funicular and foot: wooden miners' slides, an underground salt lake and a Bronze Age staircase. The Skywalk terrace is included in the ticket.

items.name: Waldbachstrub Waterfall
items.description: The three-armed waterfall at the head of the Echerntal: an easy hour's path from the square, with glacial potholes (the Gletschergarten) as a bonus en route. The crowds almost never turn this way.

items.name: Dachstein Ice Cave + 5fingers
items.description: An ice cathedral reached by the Obertraun cable car, and the five-fingered platform reaching over the abyss: a full-day reward for whoever wants Hallstatt from above.

items.name: Gosausee
items.description: The mountain lake that mirrors the Dachstein glacier: the shore loop is flat and takes an hour, the view is an alpine calendar cover. Go early — before the wind rises, the lake is a true mirror.

items.name: Sunrise at the Seelände piers
items.description: The piers just past the classic photo point belong at 6 am to the swans and you: lake, bells and mist before the village wakes — Hallstatt at its most honest.

callout.label: Skywalk tip
callout.text: Take the first funicular up to the Skywalk instead of queueing at noon: empty terrace, soft light, the village still hushed below. Enter the mine on the way down and let the stones talk for 7,000 years.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Hallstatt's trap is not malice but scale: a tiny village, a giant crowd. Know these four and both sides stay comfortable.

items.name: The midday queue at the 'postcard spot'
items.description: The classic angle becomes a selfie queue between 11:00 and 15:00; the magic dies when forty people wait behind your photo.
items.instead: Shoot the same frame before 8 am or in late afternoon; on misty mornings, the shot from the ferry beats them all anyway.

items.name: The two-hour 'seen it' tour
items.description: Rushing the square-photo-magnet triangle off a coach reduces the village to scenery; neither the mine is seen nor the lake felt.
items.instead: Stay a night, or give it at least a full day: mine in the morning, Echerntal at noon, the square at dusk — that's when the village opens.

items.name: Posing in doorways and flying drones
items.description: Stepping into gardens for photos and flying drones unasked has worn the villagers thin; drones are banned in parts of the village anyway.
items.instead: Shoot from public ground and keep distance from doors and gardens; the tourist who remembers being a guest gets the best shot through courtesy anyway.

items.name: 'Hallstatt salt' on every stall
items.description: Some of the ornate bottles on the square's stands are ordinary table salt in costume.
items.instead: Buy your salt at the Salzwelten's own shop, or from products whose label names the region; let both story and taste be real.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: In Hallstatt you don't fight the crowd, you make a deal with the clock: village before 10, mountain and lake from 10 to 4, village again after 4. Keep that rhythm and you'll never meet the crush.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: Village at dawn, mountain at noon, lake at dusk

steps.title: The square and piers — empty
steps.description: Swans, bells and a misty lake: see the village's true face before the crowds, and take the classic frame now.

steps.title: First funicular: Skywalk + salt mine
steps.description: The terrace to yourself, then a 7,000-year salt journey inside the mountain; sliding the miners' slide is permitted.

steps.title: Reinanke at a Gasthof
steps.description: The lake's fish in butter, in the calm of the parlour; let the midday crush stay outside.

steps.title: The Echerntal walk
steps.description: A sweet hour from the glacial potholes to the Waldbachstrub falls: the Hallstatt the crowds don't know.

steps.title: The Beinhaus and the upper lanes
steps.description: The silent chapel of painted skulls, then idle wandering in the narrow lanes above the square.

steps.title: Evening on the lakeshore
steps.description: The boats have gone, the terraces have calmed: watch the day's last light over a Brettljause and a beer. This is the Hallstatt of those who stayed.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the village as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: Village and mine
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: square at dawn, Skywalk, mine, Echerntal, lake at dusk.

steps.title: Dachstein day
steps.description: The ice cave and Mammut cave by the Obertraun cable car, the 5fingers platform over the abyss in the afternoon; a brave dip in the lake from the Obertraun lido on return.

steps.title: Gosausee and goodbye
steps.description: The Gosausee shore loop in the morning (leave early for the mirror hour), a village inn lunch in Gosau; a bakery stop in Bad Goisern on the way back and one last evening walk through Hallstatt to say goodbye.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Austrian German smiles more than the standard kind; these five are plenty in the valley.

items.meaning: The Austrian greeting: 'good day' — mandatory entering a shop
Please / you're welcome / here you go — German's Swiss army knife
Cheers! — no glass rises without eye contact
The warm hello-and-goodbye of the Alps — both in one word
